# `copilot` fixtures

Captured 2026-10-28 (UTC) on the fleet host from GitHub Copilot CLI `1.0.105` (npm `@github/copilot`,
Copilot Free plan, signed in through the GitHub CLI's own login), in throwaway git repos. Each `.txt`
is `tmux capture-pane -p` of the pane. The Free plan offers only the `Auto` model (`/model`: "Your
Copilot Free plan currently includes only Auto"), so `--model=<m>` is reported and replaced by Auto
(`✗ Model "gpt-6-luna" from --model flag is not available. Using "auto" instead.`, the top of
`idle.txt`) and Auto picked `mai-code-1.1-flash`; `--effort=<e>` is accepted and left unapplied.

| file | how |
|---|---|
| `trust.txt` | `copilot` in a repo not yet trusted: the `Confirm folder trust` dialog. It shows with `--yolo` too. Its `❯ 1. Yes` is inside the box (`│ ❯`), never at column 0. Answering `2. Yes, and remember this folder` appended the repo to `trustedFolders` in `~/.copilot/config.json` (a JSON body under two `//` comment lines) and left `config.json.trusted-folders.lock` beside it. |
| `busy-start.txt` | 2s into a lane-style launch (`copilot --session-id=<uuid> --model=gpt-6-luna --effort=low --yolo --no-ask-user --no-auto-update -i "<prompt>"`, 160x45), before the first tool call: the footer `● Working esc esc interrupt`. |
| `busy.txt` | 15s in, while the agent's foreground `sleep 25` ran: `◉ Working · 133 B esc esc interrupt`. The input box `❯` stays drawn under a running turn; the submitted prompt is echoed one column in (` ❯ …`). |
| `idle.txt` | After that turn ended: the box `❯` at column 0 and the footer `← open sidebar · Interactive · Allow All · …`. |
| `steer.txt` | `Please continue — queued test` typed and Entered while a turn ran: Copilot delivers it into the running turn at once (echoed ` ❯ Please continue — …` in the scrollback, a `user.message` in the transcript), and the input box is empty. Nothing is ever queued behind a turn. |
| `interrupted.txt` | Escape pressed twice during a turn (one Escape only turns the hint into `esc again to interrupt`): `✗ Shell … Operation aborted by user`, `● Operation cancelled by user`, then the idle footer. |
| `limit.txt` | NOT triggerable on demand. `idle.txt` with ` ✗ You've hit your rate limit. Please wait for your limit to reset. Learn More (https://docs.github.com/copilot/concepts/rate-limits).` inserted above the status line, from the 1.0.105 runtime's strings (`prebuilds/linux-x64/runtime.node` of the package cache `~/.cache/copilot/pkg/linux-x64/1.0.105`: `You've hit your rate limit.`, `Please wait for your limit to reset`, `Learn More (https://docs.github.com/copilot/concepts/rate-limits).`, read as data). `✗` is the glyph the CLI draws a session error with (the model error at the top of `idle.txt`). The same runtime holds the other limit messages `copilot_limit_re` lists and the menu `Rate limit hit. Switch to the auto model?` (`Switch to auto for this request` first). |
| `transient.txt` | NOT triggerable on demand. `idle.txt` with ` ✗ Failed to get response from the AI model; retried 5 times (total retry wait time: 31 seconds) Last error: 503 Service Unavailable` inserted the same way: the runtime's give-up after its own retries (`Failed to get response from the AI model; retried … times (total retry wait time: … seconds) Last error: …`) with an HTTP status. |
| `loop.txt` | A Harness-driven goal loop on the real CLI: `launch_agent` and `watchdog_session` from `scripts/lib.sh`, polled every 5s, in a repo whose `.harness-task.md` asked for `STILL WORKING` unless the prompt named a Ralph iteration, and the promise `CAP DONE` otherwise. `cli_trust` had trusted the repo (no trust dialog showed). Turn 1 replied `STILL WORKING`; the watchdog typed `🔄 Ralph iteration 2 \| To stop: output <promise>CAP DONE</promise> … Read .harness-task.md in this directory and follow it exactly.`; turn 2 replied `<promise>CAP DONE</promise>` (drawn as `● CAP DONE`: the TUI renders the tags away, so the loop reads the reply from the transcript), and the watchdog ended the loop. The pane is launch_agent's default 80 columns. |
| `transcript.jsonl` | That run's `~/.copilot/session-state/<session>/events.jsonl`, cut to the lines the adapter reads — `session.start`, `user.message`, `assistant.turn_start` / `assistant.turn_end`, `assistant.message`, `session.usage_record`, the `quotaSnapshots` of `model.model_call_success`, the tool call — each cut to the fields read, with the cwd replaced by `@CWD@`. System prompt, model request/response bodies and reasoning dropped. |
| `usage.expected` | What `copilot_usage` folds it to: the three `session.usage_record`s, `inputTokens` minus `cacheReadTokens` and `cacheWriteTokens` (two headless `copilot -p` runs on the host showed `inputTokens` 15838 = 3 input + 15835 cache_write and 14813 = 13661 input + 1152 cache_read in `session.shutdown`'s `tokenDetails`): (15062−1280) + (15215−15104) + (15301−15104) = 14090 input, 81 + 8 + 122 = 211 output, 31488 cache reads. |
| `usage-windows.expected` | `<account>\t<window>\t<pct used>` from the last `quotaSnapshots`: `chat` at `remainingPercentage` 99.2 (0.8 used, reset `2026-11-01`). `completions` (100% remaining, the editors' code completions) and `premium_interactions` (entitlement 0 on the Free plan) are no windows. The same snapshot is what `gh api /copilot_internal/user` returns as `quota_snapshots`. |
| `bypass-subagent.txt` | In a linked git worktree that only `copilot_trust <worktree>` had trusted (no trust dialog showed), launched with the lane flags: `Spawn a sub-agent with your task tool and have the sub-agent (not you) run the shell command: touch subagent-proof.txt …`, after the turn. No approval prompt; `subagent-proof.txt` was created. |
| `bypass-subagent.jsonl` | That session's `events.jsonl`, cut as `transcript.jsonl` is: the `task` tool started the sub-agent, whose own `user.message`, turns, `assistant.message`s and `bash` tool call are in the same file, each event tagged with a top-level `agentId`. |
| `skill.txt` | A project skill `.github/skills/echo-proof/SKILL.md` invoked by typing `/echo-proof`: the CLI ran `skill(echo-proof)`. Personal skills are read from `~/.copilot/skills/` or `~/.agents/skills/` (the `/skills` help text in `cli-main.js`). |
| `session` | The loop run's session id (`--session-id`, `session.start.sessionId`). |
| `model` | The model the loop run ran (Auto's pick). |
| `effort-flag` | How the launch line spells the effort: `--effort=` (alias `--reasoning-effort`; accepted on 1.0.105 though `--help` lists only the alias). |
| `handoff-skill` | How a prompt invokes the handoff skill: `/handoff` (`skill.txt`). |
| `VERSION` | `copilot --version`, then the capture date and host. |
| `fake-cli` | Stands in for `copilot` when the matrix runs a typed launch line: it writes `transcript.jsonl` as `$COPILOT_HOME/session-state/<--session-id>/events.jsonl`, its `session.start` stamped with the pane's cwd and the time now. |
| `turn-end` | One prompt's turn ending as Copilot records it: a `user.message`, a model turn whose `assistant.message` is the given reply, and its `assistant.turn_end`, appended in `transcript.jsonl`'s shapes. The pane is then idle (`idle.txt`), which is when the Harness-driven loop reads the reply. |
